title: Local finite type descends through a flat locally finitely presented surjective source map
statement: Let $X,Y,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $q:X\to Y$ be a morphism flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and surjective on underlying points, and let $h:Y\to S$ be a morphism. If $h\circ q:X\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then $h$ is locally of finite type. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis is imposed on $q$, $h$ or the schemes.

source.place: Tag 02KL (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence), locally-of-finite-type alternative; its affine algebra input is Tag 0367 (lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra).

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ containing $h(y)$, and an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ containing $y$ and contained in $h^{-1}(V)$, using the affine-open basis. Cover the open subset $q^{-1}(W)\subseteq X$ by affine opens $U_\alpha=\operatorname{Spec}B_\alpha$ of $X$ contained in $q^{-1}(W)$. The pointwise finite-type criterion shows that it suffices, for each such $y$, to prove the induced ring map $R\to A$ is of finite type. If $Y$ has no points this criterion is vacuous and the conclusion already holds.

source.place: Tag 02KL, lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence, first sentence of the proof; Schemes Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens); Morphisms Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize).

proof.text: For every $\alpha$, apply the affine-pair flatness criterion to $q$ and the pair $(U_\alpha,W)$: $A\to B_\alpha$ is flat. Apply the affine-pair finite-presentation lemma to the same pair: $A\to B_\alpha$ is of finite presentation. Apply the affine-pair finite-type criterion to $h\circ q$ and $(U_\alpha,V)$: $R\to B_\alpha$ is of finite type. These ring maps form the tower $R\to A\to B_\alpha$ since the morphism is $h\circ q$. All the opens used here are affine opens of the original schemes, so no claim about the affineness of an intersection is needed.

The morphism $q$ is open because it is flat and locally of finite presentation. Thus every $q(U_\alpha)$ is open in $Y$, hence in $W$. Surjectivity of $q$ and the covering of $q^{-1}(W)$ imply $W=\bigcup_\alpha q(U_\alpha)$. The affine scheme $W$ is quasi-compact; choose finitely many indices $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ whose images cover $W$. This uses quasi-compactness only of $W$, and imposes none on $q$ or $q^{-1}(W)$.

source.place: Tag 02KL, proof, openness and finite affine selection; Morphisms Tag 01UA (lemma-fppf-open); Algebra Tag 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Form $Z=\coprod_{i=1}^nU_{\alpha_i}$ and the morphisms $q_Z:Z\to W$, $p_Z:Z\to V$ induced by the component maps; then $p_Z=(h|_W)\circ q_Z$ by the coproduct universal property. The components are pairwise disjoint open subschemes covering $Z$. By the finite-coproduct spectrum identification, $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=\prod_{i=1}^nB_{\alpha_i}$, with the specified component maps. At a point of component $U_{\alpha_i}$ the local-ring map of $q_Z$ is the local-ring map of $q$ at that point, because both source and target have merely been restricted to open neighbourhoods. Thus $q_Z$ is flat by the stalkwise definition. Each component is an affine neighbourhood with finitely presented $A$-algebra by step 2, so the pointwise definition gives that $q_Z$ is locally of finite presentation. Each component also has finite-type $R$-algebra, so the pointwise finite-type criterion gives that $p_Z$ is locally of finite type. Finally $q_Z$ is surjective by the chosen finite image cover.

source.place: Tag 02KL, proof, replacement by a finite affine coproduct; Schemes Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue, lemma-glue-schemes), applied to disjoint gluing; Morphisms Tags 01U3 (definition-flat), 01TP (definition-finite-presentation), 01T2.

proof.text: Apply the affine-pair criteria to the full affine source $Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and the full affine targets $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. From flatness and local finite presentation of $q_Z$ obtain that $A\to B$ is flat and of finite presentation. From local finite type of $p_Z$ obtain that the composite $R\to B$ is of finite type. The tower $R\to A\to B$ is exactly that of the two maps constructed in step 4, so its composite ring map agrees with that induced by $p_Z$.

source.place: Tag 02KL, proof, final affine reduction; Morphisms Tags 01U5, 01TQ, 01T2.

proof.text: For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset A$, surjectivity of $q_Z$ supplies a prime $\mathfrak n\subset B$ whose inverse image is $\mathfrak m$. Every image of an element of $\mathfrak m$ lies in $\mathfrak n$, hence $\mathfrak mB\subseteq\mathfrak n\ne B$. Thus every extended maximal ideal is proper. Together with flatness of $A\to B$ from step 5, the cited faithful-flatness criterion implies that $A\to B$ is faithfully flat. If $A$ is the zero ring the condition on maximal ideals is empty, and the same criterion still applies.

source.place: Tag 02KL, final affine reduction; Algebra Tag 00HP (lemma-ff), implication (4) to (1); compare Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings).

proof.text: Apply the ring-tower descent lemma to $R\to A\to B$: step 5 gives finite type of $R\to B$ and finite presentation of $A\to B$, while step 6 gives faithful flatness of $A\to B$. Conclude that $R\to A$ is of finite type. For each $y\in Y$, the affine pair $(W,V)$ chosen in step 1 now satisfies the pointwise finite-type criterion for $h$. Therefore $h$ is locally of finite type.

source.place: Tag 02KL (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence), locally-of-finite-type conclusion, using Tag 0367 (lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra) and Morphisms Tag 01T2.
